subject: Apogee Networks: capacity entitlement and headroom plan for Dedicated
messages:

Subject: Initial sizing input for Dedicated commit

Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Ravi and I pulled together our initial expected usage profile and attached a quick spreadsheet (summary below) so we can sync on Dedicated sizing and an entitlement proposal. High level: we expect a large spike at product launch and a steady baseline after ramp.

Summary (peak vs baseline):
- Peak (launch windows): ~1,200 completions / minute for 30 minutes per hour (bursty schedule)
- Baseline (steady day): ~250 completions / minute
- Avg tokens per completion: 300 tokens (conservative)
- Model: will start on a top-tier 13B-ish instruction model (we're model-agnostic but need real numbers)
- SLO: p95 response latency < 500ms (total time to first token is most important)

Specific asks:
1) Can you map these numbers to tokens/sec and give a conservative Dedicated slab (GPU count + SKU) for a 12-month commit?
2) What headroom do you recommend for burst tolerance and regional failover?
3) Any quick ideas to reduce committed footprint (quantization, caching, routing)?

I've attached the spreadsheet with minute-by-minute projections and expected growth for Q4.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Patel
Head of AI Integrations, Apogee Networks

Hi Maya / Ravi —

Thanks for the spreadsheet — that was helpful. I ran a quick capacity translation and sketched a conservative entitlement + headroom plan. Below is the reasoning and the numbers we recommend for a first committed slab with an add-on burst pool.

Key math (conservative assumptions):
- Peak completions/min: 1,200 -> tokens/min = 1,200 * 300 = 360,000 tokens/min -> tokens/sec = 6,000 t/s
- Baseline completions/min: 250 -> 250 * 300 = 75,000 tokens/min -> 1,250 t/s

Model & per-GPU throughput estimates (these are test-derived approximations for the 13B-class instruction model we discussed):
- H100-80GB (fp16/quant hybrid): ~2,200 tokens/sec sustained per GPU at typical batching and 512-1,024 token sequences
- A100-80GB (mixed workload): ~1,400 tokens/sec per GPU

Capacity sizing (no cache, conservative latency target):
- To sustain peak 6,000 t/s: need ~3 x H100 (3*2,200=6,600 t/s) -> leaves ~10% raw headroom
- We recommend initial committed slab = 4 x H100 to provide ~47% headroom on raw tokens/sec (4*2,200=8,800 t/s) and buffer for tail latency and model variance
- Equivalent with A100s would be ~5 x A100 (5*1,400=7,000 t/s) but we prefer H100s for latency and quant overhead

Recommended configuration (first 12-month commit):
- Committed: 4 x H100 (primary slab)
- Burst: additional 2 x H100 as on-demand burst pool for scheduled launch windows and regional failover
- Autoscaling policy: keep baseline routing on committed slab; allow burst pool to route only when queue depth > 200ms or tokens/sec sustained > 65% of committed capacity for >2 minutes

Headroom rationale:
- 4x H100 gives you ~8,800 t/s raw. With auto-batching and prefix caching we expect practical delivered capacity to improve by ~25-35% for repeat prompts (hot paths), so effective headroom for typical production traffic is higher than raw numbers suggest.
- Operationally we advise reserving 25-30% of slab for background tasks (warmups, evals, retries) — that's already reflected in the 4x recommendation.

Options to reduce committed footprint (tradeoffs):
- Quantized 8-bit variants: ~20-30% more tokens/sec per GPU but slightly higher decode variance; we can A/B a quantized variant behind a canary to measure quality impact
- KV / prefix caching: if a portion of traffic is prompt-reuse (e.g., templates, system prompts), caching can cut token generation by 20-40% for those flows
- Routing to cheaper region/model for non-interactive bulk jobs (embeddings, long-form batch jobs)

Latency SLO notes:
- The p95 < 500ms is achievable with the 4x H100 config if we control max sequence lengths and prioritize first-token latency in the runtime. Heavy tails (very long completions) should be routed to the burst pool or to a fallback smaller model with lower latency requirement.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben and I will prepare a formal entitlement sheet (GPU SKUs, monthly committed cost, billing cadence).
2) Agree on scheduled launch windows where we allow burst capacity to avoid over-committing.
3) Run a short live canary with quantized variant to measure quality delta vs perf gains.

I'm attaching a quick topology diagram and the token math workbook with per-minute scenarios. Will follow up with cost estimates.

Sergio
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in a few cost and ops details to make the proposal actionable. Sergio, good calc — a couple of adjustments / clarifications from the ops side below.

Cost heuristics (examples for sizing discussion only):
- 4 x H100 committed slab -> estimated platform + infra blended cost to customer: ~$95k - $130k / month depending on region, network egress, and support tier (we'll pin exact number in the commercial sheet)
- Burst 2 x H100 on-call pool -> additional metered fee (only used when burst consumed)

Operational tweaks we recommend to improve SLO and reduce commit:
- Warm KV cache alignment: Warm the most common system prompts during peak windows; this frequently knocks 15-25% off token demand when prompts are templated
- Sequence-length caps: For interactive routes, enforce a soft cap (e.g., 1,200 tokens), and route edge cases to a background job queue
- Canary flow: start with 90/10 routing to quantized model for non-critical customers in the first 48 hours after launch

Procurement/Legal notes for Maya / Ravi:
- We can structure the 12-month commit as a monthly recurring commitment with a target tokens/month quota and a burst meter.
- Standard enterprise SLA: 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated pools; pricing tier and credits are negotiable with a minimum commitment threshold (we will send a redline-friendly term sheet)

Action items / ask:
- Maya / Ravi: confirm your launch-day windows (dates + expected 30-minute spike schedule) and any region preference for primary slab (we default to us-west-2 unless you need eu-west-1)
- Sergio: please add the commercial numbers and a clear definition of burst activation thresholds in the entitlement sheet

Ben
Director, Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
